official.deadline_note: No central deadline is published. Recruitment is conducted by the embassies of Japan in target countries upon the recommendation of official overseas recommending organisations, and the type and field of application can differ from country to country, so the timetable is set country by country.
official.application_cycle: Country-by-country recruitment through Japanese embassies and official overseas recommending organisations, at timings that differ by country and region
official.status_note: YLP is one of the seven MEXT scholarship types and is recruited through the embassies of Japan in target countries; applicants must check with their embassy whether an opening exists in the type and field they wish to apply for.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The official MEXT scholarship portal lists YLP benefits as a JPY 242,000 monthly scholarship, tuition exempted, and round-trip travel expenses (airfare) provided.

official.citizenship_residency: Applicants come from the YLP target countries, recruited through the embassies of Japan and official overseas recommending organisations.
official.international_eligibility: Aimed at young leaders from Asia and other countries who are expected to play an active role there.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The type and field of application differ from country to country; applicants must check with the embassy whether there is an opening in the type and field they wish to apply for.
official.description: Young Leaders Program (YLP) Students is the seventh type of the Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship. It funds a one-year master's course at a Japanese graduate school for university or college graduates with practical work experience and for young public administrators who are expected to play an active role in Asia and other countries. MEXT's portal lists the scholarship as JPY 242,000 per month with tuition exempted and round-trip airfare provided.

not_confirmed: Application deadline or recruitment calendar (set country by country by each Japanese embassy and recommending organisation)
English or Japanese language requirement (set by the recruiting embassy and host graduate school, not published by MEXT for YLP)
verification.notes: The official studyinjapan.go.jp MEXT scholarship page was fetched on 2026-10-10: the types table confirms YLP at JPY 242,000 per month, tuition exempted, round-trip travel expenses provided, one-year duration, under-40 eligibility, and the footnote that YLP uses recommendations from official overseas recommending organisations.

applicant_utility.summary: YLP pays the largest MEXT monthly allowance, JPY 242,000, plus tuition exemption and round-trip airfare for a one-year master's course, and it exists specifically for early-career leaders with work experience. The catch is access: you cannot apply directly, and the only door is a recommendation from an official overseas recommending organisation in a target country, routed through the Japanese embassy. Before anything else, verify that your country runs a YLP intake in the current year and in a field matching your background, because openings genuinely vary by country.
applicant_utility.best_fit: University or college graduates under 40 with practical work experience, including young public administrators, from countries where Japan's embassy runs a YLP intake.
application_readiness_checklist: Ask the Japanese embassy in your country whether a YLP intake is open this year and in which fields
Identify the official overseas recommending organisation that handles YLP nominations in your country and ask for its internal deadline
Assemble documentary proof of both your degree and your years of practical work experience
Prepare for document screening, an interview and an essay writing test at the embassy stage
Line up the documents your chosen graduate school will need for master's admission
common_rejection_risks: Assuming a direct application is possible and missing the recommending-organisation route entirely
Your country has no YLP intake in your field this year, which no amount of preparation can fix
Falling at the embassy's initial screening, which includes an essay writing component
Being over the in-principle under-40 age limit at the time of application
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Beyond the monthly allowance and airfare, applicants fund their own relocation, settlement and personal expenses; MEXT publishes no additional allowances for this category.
document_audit: Work-experience evidence must match the 'practical work experience' requirement, not just a degree
The recommending organisation's endorsement is a hard gate: files without it never reach the embassy shortlist
Expect the embassy's own document list to override any generic checklist you find elsewhere
alerts: YLP is the only one of the seven MEXT types that is neither embassy-recommended nor university-recommended
No preliminary Japanese language training is provided for this category
The timetable differs by country and region, so guidance from another country's applicants can mislead you on timing
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Get recommended by the official overseas recommending organisation, register with the Japanese embassy, pass document screening plus interview and essay, then await the YLP Committee's decision and master's placement.

official.deadline_note: JASSO publishes no deadline: 'Please ask school you plan to enroll in. We do not accept applications directly from students.' The deadline is the school's own pre-arrival admission and scholarship nomination deadline.
official.application_cycle: Twice a year, matching Japanese enrolment cycles: spring enrolment (April) and autumn enrolment (September or October); JASSO publishes the eligible school and department lists for each cycle.
official.status_note: JASSO publishes eligible school lists for each cycle (spring and autumn enrolment); applications are handled entirely through the school the applicant plans to enrol in.
benefits: 12 months of support for students enrolled in April (April of the year of enrolment to the following March)
6 months of support for students enrolled in September or October (October of the year of enrolment to the following March)
eligibility: Privately-financed international student who is not a Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship holder
Has received pre-arrival admission to an eligible school for the relevant reservation category
Plans to enrol as a full-time student; research students, trainees, non-degree students, advanced course students, special course students, auditing students and special students are excluded
Graduate level: enrolling in a graduate school in Japan in April (September or October for autumn enrolment) using pre-arrival admission

EJU exam or English courses: enrolling in an undergraduate school, junior college, college of technology (3rd grade or upper) or specialized course in a specialized training college using pre-arrival admission
Faces financial difficulties and has an excellent academic and character record
requirements: The procedure must be completed through the school the applicant plans to enrol in; JASSO does not accept applications directly from students
The school must be on the eligible list for the relevant reservation category for that enrolment cycle
For the EJU exam category JASSO uses the registered-school list as of 1 October for spring enrolment or 1 April for September/October enrolment, which may differ from the web list
The student must enrol as a full-time student under the programme's definition

Pre-arrival admission confirmation from that school
Academic and character records required by the school
Documents listed by the school for its scholarship nomination
selection_criteria: JASSO's stated objectives: to ease students' financial concerns about arrival and studies in Japan, promote pre-arrival admission and improve the level of learning
Targets privately-financed international students with excellent academic and character records who face financial difficulties
Practical selection is carried out through the school
coverage: Monthly stipend of JPY 48,000 only; no tuition waiver or travel benefit is published for this programme
JASSO notes the amount may change from one academic year to another

Ask that school to run the scholarship nomination for the reservation programme

The school submits the nomination to JASSO
Receive the stipend from enrolment for the period stated for the enrolment month
official.application_route: Obtain pre-arrival admission at a listed school and apply through that school, which nominates you to JASSO; you cannot apply to JASSO yourself.
official.citizenship_residency: For privately-financed international students holding pre-arrival admission to a Japanese institution.
official.international_eligibility: Open to privately-financed international students (excluding MEXT scholarship holders) with pre-arrival admission.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Three reservation categories: graduate level, EJU exam (non-graduate schools registered with JASSO), and English courses (undergraduate courses awarding degrees with classes conducted only in English).
official.duration: 12 months for April enrollees (April to the following March); 6 months for September or October enrollees (October to the following March)
official.description: JASSO's reservation programme for the Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship supports privately-financed international students who have received pre-arrival admission in Japan and face financial difficulties. JASSO states its objectives are to ease students' financial concerns about arrival and studies in Japan, promote pre-arrival admission and improve the level of learning.
official.program_type: Reservation programme for the MEXT Honors Scholarship, by pre-arrival admission
official.english_requirement: No language test is set by JASSO. The English courses reservation category is restricted to schools whose relevant undergraduate courses award a degree or associate degree with classes conducted only in English, so English-medium study is a feature of that category rather than a test requirement.

not_confirmed: Application deadline (set by each school's pre-arrival admission and nomination timetable)
Whether a specific school participates in the current cycle
verification.notes: JASSO's official reservation-programme page was fetched on 2026-10-10: monthly stipend JPY 48,000, 12-month (April) and 6-month (September/October) periods, apply-through-the-school rule, the three reservation categories and the eligible-school-list mechanics were read directly from the page.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a modest JPY 48,000 monthly stipend for the first year in Japan, reserved for privately-financed students who already hold pre-arrival admission at a JASSO-listed school and can show financial hardship. Nothing is paid toward tuition or flights, so treat it as settling-in help rather than funding. The decisive step happens before you arrive: your school must run the nomination, so confirm at the admission stage that it participates in this reservation programme for your intake.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Privately-financed students with pre-arrival admission to a listed Japanese school who need help with the first months of living costs in Japan.
application_readiness_checklist: Before accepting an admission offer, ask the school in writing whether it nominates students for this reservation programme and for which category
Check your school appears on JASSO's eligible list for the cycle matching your enrolment month (April vs September/October)
Prepare evidence of financial difficulty in the form the school requests
Confirm you fit the programme's full-time student definition - research students, trainees, auditors and non-degree students are excluded
Ask the school for its internal nomination deadline and submit well before it
common_rejection_risks: Assuming JASSO accepts direct applications; it does not
Choosing a school that is not on the eligible list for the relevant reservation category and cycle
Being enrolled as a research student, trainee, auditor or special student instead of a regular full-time student
Applying for the autumn-enrolment cycle against the spring list, or vice versa
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition, admission and entrance fees, flights, insurance and most living costs; the stipend is only JPY 48,000 per month for 6 or 12 months.
document_audit: The pre-arrival admission evidence must come from the school, and the school's own scholarship application is separate from your admission file
JASSO's eligible-school list for EJU-based reservation is fixed as of 1 October or 1 April and may differ from the list published on the web page at the time you check it
Because the amount can change each academic year, verify the figure for your intake year with your school
alerts: Support stops after 12 months (April entry) or 6 months (September/October entry) - plan finances for the following year early
Holding a MEXT scholarship disqualifies you; this programme is only for privately-financed students
The English-courses category only applies to degree programmes taught entirely in English
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Secure pre-arrival admission at a listed school, ask that school to nominate you through its internal scholarship process, and the school submits the nomination to JASSO.
